about.title: Greenfield Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Greenfield sees its share of collisions on corridors like Oak Avenue, El Camino Real, Elm Avenue, and Walnut Avenue, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. In a recent year, the city recorded 25 injury collisions and 27 people injured. Behind each of those numbers is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a lot of uncertainty about what comes next. We handle personal injury claims and can review your situation, explain your options under California law, and manage communications with insurance companies on your behalf. Whether your crash happened at a busy Greenfield intersection or on a quieter stretch of road, having an attorney who understands local conditions and Monterey County procedures can make the process less overwhelming.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Dealing With Insurance

items.title: California's Deadline Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government entity (like a city road defect) contributed to your accident, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Missing it can end your case before it starts, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce — Not Erase — Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. We can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, but anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. Our team can advise you on what to share and help preserve evidence like photos, witness contacts, and crash reports before they disappear.

items.question: How much does it cost to speak with an attorney about my case?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning we only collect a fee if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.

items.question: I was in a crash on El Camino Real in Greenfield — do I need to talk to the other driver's insurance company right away?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often wiser to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements to shift blame or downplay injuries. Speaking with us first can help protect your position.

items.question: What if the crash happened at a Greenfield intersection with no clear fault?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rules allow you to pursue compensation even in situations where fault seems shared or unclear. We can help gather evidence — like traffic camera footage, witness statements, or the police report — to establish what actually happened. Acting quickly matters, since evidence and memories fade over time.
